mappings.note: Monazite sands of Kerala as the source of thorium: the location of a named mineral, LO-1. Not LO-2, since no energy source is being evaluated here, only where the mineral lies.
Nagercoil and Jaisalmer are the chapter's wind-energy examples, so this is the non-conventional-source half of LO-2, not the mineral distribution of LO-1.
Which pair of states holds most petroleum deposits: the distribution of a mineral fuel, LO-1. LO-2 would fit an item weighing petroleum against a renewable alternative.
Identifies a non-metallic mineral. The metallic/non-metallic classification has no LO in this frame (LO-1 is about distribution), so the recall competency is cited.
Aluminium comes from bauxite: ore-to-metal recall. Not C-2.3-LO-15, which requires the risk of industry's dependence on a mineral to be analysed rather than the ore named.
Where uranium and thorium occur: mineral distribution, LO-1, even though the use is nuclear power.
Where tidal energy is produced: a non-conventional energy source, LO-2.
Where tertiary coals occur (the north-eastern states): distribution of a mineral fuel, LO-1. Contrast qid:106040 and qid:106041, which ask about coal grades rather than location.

Why the electrical and electronics industries need mica is precisely the industrial dependence on a mineral that LO-15 asks about. Contrast qid:106046, which asks for mica's own properties and takes C-2.1.
Limestone as the basic raw material of the cement industry: industry's dependence on a steady mineral supply, LO-15, not the location of limestone (LO-1).
Names lodes, the larger occurrences of minerals in igneous and metamorphic rocks. A mode-of-occurrence term; LO-1 is about where minerals are, not how they occur.
The state with the largest wind farm cluster: a non-conventional energy source, LO-2.
India's oldest oil-producing state (Assam): distribution of a mineral fuel, LO-1.
Geothermal energy at Manikaran: a non-conventional source, LO-2.
Which iron-ore belt holds the Kudremukh mines: mineral distribution, LO-1.
India's largest copper producer: mineral distribution by state, LO-1.
Which mineral comes largely from ocean water (common salt, magnesium, bromine): an occurrence-and-source question, so the distribution LO rather than the energy LO.
Anthracite as the highest grade of hard coal: classification of coal by rank. No LO covers the grading; LO-2 is about evaluating energy sources, not ranking them.
The low-carbon, high-moisture, low-heat grade (lignite or peat): the other end of the coal grading of qid:106040, same recall level.

Why sugar mills shifted to the southern and western states. This item is MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES content misfiled into Minerals and Energy Resources; the industrial-location LO belongs to another chapter's frame, so the data-analysis competency is cited.
The importance of manufacturing industries. Also misfiled from Manufacturing Industries; no LO in this mineral-and-energy frame reaches it, so the analysis competency is the honest level.
Which mineral is not found in veins and lodes: modes of occurrence, the same recall target as qid:106033.
Duplicate of qid:106036 with the Parvati Valley named; geothermal energy as a non-conventional source, LO-2.
An essential feature of mica (its dielectric strength and insulating property): the mineral's own properties, so C-2.1. LO-15 is cited at qid:106031, where the industrial dependence is what is asked.
Which feature is untrue of copper: the mineral's properties and uses, recall level, as with qid:106046.
